title: Odile and the Crown
premise: Beatrix Delacroix keeps two lives: by day, a ledger-keeper for the Guild of Impossible Things; by night, a memory-thief who erases her own tracks by stealing her recollections of each job. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish in a single night, she realizes the Guild's founder traded away the sky itself to buy immortality—and that the memory proving it now lives in her head, stolen from a dying client. Hunted by the Guild's enforcers and shadowed by a disgraced warden who remembers her face, Beatrix must decide whether to restore the stolen memories of thousands of conscripted wardens, which would shatter her own identity and expose her crimes, or stay silent while the ancient enemy beyond the wards gathers. She chooses truth: she gives the wardens back their memories, loses most of her own in the exchange, and the restored wardens relight the stars at the cost of the founder's life and Beatrix's past. The book ends with her standing under a returned dawn, keeping a single new memory—her own name, written in her own hand.
about_author: E. M. Underhill is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed estate records before turning to fiction. They write fantasies about people who keep dangerous paperwork, and live quietly with a cat who is never named in interviews.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Crimes
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. We meet her double life: meticulous guild ledgers by day, a memory-theft job by night in which she steals a dying warden's final recollections. She erases her own memory of the theft, as always. The chapter ends with her waking with blood on her sleeve and no idea why—an unsettling hook establishing the cost of her method.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The border wards fail and the sky goes black; the city panics while the Guild pretends business as usual. Beatrix finds a fragment of the warden's memory surfacing in her mind—wards don't simply fall. Emotional beat: dread beneath practiced calm, as her invisibility begins to crack.

chapters.title: A Warden Who Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, with a closing scene from Cassian Vey's. Disgraced warden Cassian Vey corners her—he saw her face the night of the theft and has been hunting the same truth. Uneasy alliance forms. Beat: reluctant trust; two liars negotiating honesty.

chapters.title: The Founder's Bargain
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Decoding the ledgers, she discovers the Guild founder traded the wardens' memories to something beyond the border in exchange for unaging life. The stars were collateral. Beat: horror of comprehension—the paperwork she kept was the weapon.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. He leads her to a river-vault of confiscated memories, including a shard proving the conscripted wardens were erased, not paid. Beatrix realizes restoring them means surrendering her own stolen stores—her safety net and much of herself. Beat: temptation of silence.

chapters.title: The Guild's Long Hand
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The Guild's enforcers raze her lodgings; her mentor, Mistress Ivo, reveals she has always known what Beatrix is and offers protection in exchange for the warden's memory. Beat: betrayal wrapped in kindness; loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Archive
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. They burn the false ledgers to buy time, but the fire exposes the vault to the Guild, and Ivo dies covering their escape, whispering that the enemy beyond the wards is already crossing. Beat: grief and guilt—the cost of choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Enemy at the Edge
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the broken border they witness the ancient enemy wearing the faces of forgotten wardens. Beatrix understands: only restored memories can call the true wardens back to their posts. Beat: terror transmuted into resolve; the secret becomes a burden she refuses to carry alone.

chapters.title: The Giving Back
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax at the river-vault. Beatrix pours every stolen memory back into their owners, unraveling her own past with each restoration. The founder arrives to stop them; the returning wardens' collective memory unmakes his bargain and his life. Cassian holds the line as Beatrix gives away the last of herself. Beat: sacrifice as the final act of loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Her Own Name
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, sparse and quiet. The stars return. She wakes with almost nothing—no history, few skills intact—but a note in her own handwriting: her name, and one sentence of warning for whoever she becomes. Cassian stays. Beat: bittersweet resolution; identity rebuilt from a single honest page.
